aun: aun — even, besides · also aun — yet, still (aun vea el dia 'may I yet see the day') · also 'even though' (= aunque; aun de lo que diessen oviessen grand ganançia, Pidal's reading)
vea: veer — may I/he see (present subjunctive 1st/3rd sg.; = vea)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora) · also una grant ora — a long while (Pidal 'un gran rato'; = un buen rato)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran) · also do + se, 'where … (he might)' with a subjunctive (non vido … dos alçasse 'he saw nowhere he might hide', Pidal 'donde se escondiese')
tanto: tanto — so much, so great · tanto quanto + subjunctive 'as long as' (tanto quanto yo biva 'as long as I live') · also tanto — 'so many' before a masc. sg. noun used collectively (tanto palafré, tanto buen pendón 'so many a palfrey, so many a good banner'; = tantos)
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
una: uno/una — one, a (fem.) · also a una — together, as one (adverbial; hivan a una compaña 'they went together'; a una grant ondrança 'together with great honor'; = juntos)
tornados: tornar — turned back, returned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with los 'them'; a los moros dentro los an tornados 'they have put the Moors back inside'; = vueltos, devueltos) · also tornar — turned back, returned (intransitive, with ser; tornados son 'they have turned back'; = vueltos)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
assi: assí — thus, so (printed assi, unaccented; = así; Minaya Álvar Fáñez assi era llegado 'Minaya had thus arrived')
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
pero: Pero — Peter (San Pero = San Pedro, the saint of the monastery) · also Pero — Pedro, Per Vermudoz (don Pero, the Cid's vassal)
quomo: commo — as (variant spelling, Pidal's Qu[o]mo; = como)
se: se — himself/herself/itself (reflexive pronoun) · also se — passive 'is, are' (cómmo se gana el pan 'how bread is earned'; = se, passive-reflexive) · also se — ethic/intensive dative 'for himself, with his own eyes' (él se lo vío con los ojos 'he saw it himself')
ferrando: Ferrando — Fernando (Fernando González, the other infante of Carrión; = Fernando)
plogo: plazer — it pleased (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = plugo, modern plació)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront') · also a — 'with' of instrument (a dientes las tomó 'with his teeth he took them'; = con)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus) · also los sos 'his own men' (possessive with article as noun; en todos los sos 'among all his men')
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda) · also si non — 'except, but for' (si non a estos cavalleros 'except these knights'; = salvo) · also si — 'so', optative, = sí, with the present subjunctive in an adjuration (si vos vala el Criador 'so may the Creator help you')
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
quisiere: querer — shall wish (future subjunctive 3rd sg.; = quisiere)
padre: padre — father · el Padre santo, God the Father
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
canpo: canpo — field, battlefield (en canpo 'in the field, in battle'; = campo)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
diziendo: dezir — saying (gerund; diziendo Minaya 'Minaya says', the gerund standing for a finite verb of speech; = diciendo)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
allegando: allegar — gathering, coming together, drawing near (gerund; se van allegando 'they come gathering, assembling'; = allegándose, juntándose)
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment') · also de — 'with, from' of the means or source (diziendo de la boca 'saying with his mouth'; de cuer les pesa 'it grieves them from the heart') · also de que 'of whom, of which' (relative after a noun; de moros de que non avien sabor 'of Moors they had no taste for')
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
atamores: atamor — drum (pl.; also atambor, from Arabic, with the article al- assimilated; ante roído de atamores 'at the din of the drums'; = tambores)
sonando: sonar — sounding, ringing out, being spoken of (gerund; sonando van 'keep ringing out', ir + gerund, of his fame; = sonando)
maravilla: maravilla — wonder, marvel (noun; = maravilla) · also aver a maravilla — to marvel at, hold a wonder (a maravilla lo han 'they marvel at it')
dessos: de + essos — of, under those (preposition de + demonstrative essos masc. pl.; en poder dessos 'in the power of those'; = de esos)
cristianos: cristiano — Christian(s) (masc. pl.); moros nin cristianos / cristianos alone idiomatically = 'anyone at all'
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain) · also ca non — 'and not that' (Pidal 'y no que'; cuédanse que es almofalla, ca non vienen con mandado 'they think it is an army, and not that they come with a message')
llegados: llegar — arrived, come (past part. masc. pl. after the auxiliary seer; quando son llegados 'when they have come'; = llegados)
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
entre: entre — between, among; entre X e Y 'X and Y together'
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession') · also por — 'about, after' with preguntar (por el rey tómanse a preguntar 'they begin to ask after the king'); por + infinitive 'for … to' (por … vençer reyes, 'for … to defeat kings')
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly' · God's will (commo fo tu voluntad 'as was your will'); de toda voluntad 'with all one's heart' · also de buena voluntad 'gladly, willingly' (the formula of assent); a toda su voluntad 'wholly to his satisfaction, at his will' · also damor e de voluntad 'with love and good will, gladly' (the formula of assent)
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
per: Per — Pero, short for Pedro (Per Vermudoz = Pedro Bermúdez, a vassal of the Cid)
sobrino: sobrino — nephew (= sobrino; so sobrino 'his nephew')
fernando: Fernando — Fernando, one of the two Infantes of Carrión (also Ferrando; = Fernando)
cosa: cosa — thing; nulla cosa 'anything' (after a negative, 'nothing'; = cosa)
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon') · also mas mucho — 'more' (mucho as a comparative = más: mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; Pidal)
amo: amar — I love (present 1st sg.; el que yo quiero e amo 'he whom I want and love'; = amo)
fincarán: fincar — they will remain (future 3rd pl.; = quedarán, closest)
digo: dezir — I say (present 1st sg.; yo non vos digo nada 'I say nothing to you'; = digo)
caridad: caridad — charity, mercy; por caridad 'for charity's sake, I beg you' (= caridad)
ifantes: infante — young nobleman, son of a noble house (pl., spelt Ifantes; = infantes)
abrán: aver — they will have (future 3rd pl.; = habrán); abrán a far 'they will have to do' · also abrán de + inf. 'will have to, are bound to' (a bien abrán de venir 'will come to good'; = habrán de)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien) · also qui — who? (interrogative; ¿qui los podrié contar? 'who could count them?'; = quién) · also qui after a negative — 'anyone who, one to' (non ha qui tomallos 'there is nobody to take them'; = quien)
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
poco: poco — little · also a poco que — 'shortly after' (a poco que viniestes 'a little after you came')
m: me — me, to me (elided form of me before a vowel, querer m'a = me querrá)
incal: incaler — it matters (present 3rd sg., impersonal, apocopated; a mi non m'incal 'it does not matter to me', = importa)
ferir: ferir — to strike, attack (infinitive; vayámoslos ferir 'let us go and strike them'; = herir)
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente) · also firme' — firmes, 'firm, steadfast' (adjective plural, final s dropped; firme' son los moros 'the Moors are firm', i.e. still holding their ground)
mientre: mientre — adverb-forming suffix, 'in a manner' (Latin mente; fuerte mientre = fuertemente)
çaga: çaga — rear, rearguard (a la çaga 'at the rear'; = zaga)
tengades: tener — (that) you hold (present subjunctive 2nd pl., -ades; non lo tengades a mal 'do not take it ill', prohibition; = tengáis)
cueta: cueta — distress, trouble, urgent need (= cuita, 'grief, trouble'; closest apuro)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
podredes: poder — you will be able (future 2nd pl., syncopated for poderedes; hi los podredes fallar 'you will be able to find them there'; = podréis)
huviar: huviar — to help, come to the aid of (infinitive; nin los vino huviar 'nor did he come to help them', Pidal 'ni les vino a ayudar'; = ayudar, socorrer)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
mynaya: Minaya — spelling of Minaya with y (see minaya), the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
canpeador: Campeador — spelling variant with n for m (copyist's spelling) of Campeador, the Cid's epithet
batalla: batalla — battle (= batalla; exir a batalla 'to sally out to battle')
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
avedes: aver — you have (2nd pl. present, -edes; perfect auxiliary with a participle, me avedes mandado 'you have granted me'; = habéis)
parte: parte — part, side (de parte de los moros 'on the Moors' side'; = parte) · also partir (se) — he parts, leaves (present 3rd sg. of partir, with non se le: que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'; = se aparta) · also partir — it divides, separates (present 3rd sg., transitive; la sierra, que las otras tierras parte 'the sierra that divides the other lands'; = separa) · also parte — share, place, footing (with dar: dovos … parte 'I give you a place', Pidal 'os doy acogida en mi reino'; = parte, acogida)
part: part — share, portion (noun; = parte) · also part — side (del otra part 'on the other side'; = parte) · also a part — aside, apart (a part salidos son 'they have gone aside')
debdo: debdo — debt, obligation (= deuda); aver en debdo 'to be bound by a vow'
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de) · also non ha qui + inf. — 'there is no one to' (impersonal ha 'there is'; non ha qui tomallos 'there is no one to take them'; = no hay quien) · also ha — of time elapsed, 'it is, it has been' (Pocos días ha … que 'it is a few days since'; = hace)
cada: cada — each, every (= cada; a cada uno 'to each one')
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one' · el uno ... el otro 'the one ... the other' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró) · also lo uno … lo otro 'one part … the other part' (neuter; lo uno adebdan e lo otro pagavan 'part they owe and part they paid')
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
auze: auze — luck, fortune (vuestra auze 'your good fortune'; a word of augury, usually traced to Latin avis 'bird'; rare, and its exact sense not certain; closest suerte, ventura)
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
ayamos: aver — let us have (present subjunctive 1st pl.; ayamos vistas 'let us hold a meeting'; = hayamos)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more' · also más por espacio — 'later, at more leisure' (más 'further'; por espacio 'in good time')
afevos: afevos — behold, here is/are (presentative, a + fe + vos; = he aquí, ahí tenéis)
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
armado: armar — armed (past part.; armado es mio Çid 'my Cid is armed', ser as auxiliary; = armado)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later' · also por al 'otherwise, for any other reason' (non passará por al 'it will not be otherwise'); a mí mandedes al 'order me something else', give me another charge (the likelier reading of a terse line)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
siempre: siempre — always, forever; por siempre 'for ever'
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos · santa — holy (adjective; santa Trinidad 'the Holy Trinity', santa María madre 'holy Mary, (thy) mother', the Virgin) · also Santa María — the church (cathedral) of Valencia, Don Jerome's see, where the drums are to be hung (colgar los han en Santa María madre del Criador)
esso: esso — that (neuter demonstrative; esso con esto 'that together with this'; = eso)
mi: mi — my (unstressed possessive) · also mi — me (stressed pronoun after a preposition; por mi 'on my behalf'; = mí)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land · earth (fezist çielo e tierra 'you made heaven and earth'; por tierra 'on earth')
buscare: buscar — shall seek (future subjunctive 3rd sg.; qui nos buscare 'whoever shall seek us'; = buscare, tense obsolete)
sabor: sabor — pleasure, wish; a so sabor 'at his (their) pleasure' · also por sabor de 'out of a wish to please, for the sake of' (por sabor de mio Çid 'to please the Cid')
avía: aver — there was, it had (imperfect 3rd sg.; que non i avía hart 'for there was no flaw in it'; = había)
algún: alguno — some, any (apocopated before a noun; = algún)
moro: moro — Moor, Muslim (noun; el moro Avengalvón 'the Moor Avengalvón'; = moro)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating · also a las manos tomar 'to take by the hand' (a las manos les tomó, Pidal 'los tomó de la mano')
querría: querer — I would like, would want (conditional 1st sg.)
ondrar: ondrar — to honour (infinitive; ondrar vos hemos 'we shall honour you', infinitive + vos + auxiliary, split future; = honrar)
feridas: ferida — blow, wound (fem. pl.; las feridas primeras 'the first blows'; = heridas)
ir: ir — to go (infinitive; = ir) · ir + gerund in a split future (ir nos hemos pagando 'we shall go on paying ourselves'; = nos iremos pagando) · also ir + infinitive in a split future (ir los hemos fferir 'we shall go and strike them'; = los iremos a herir)
trayo: traer — I carry, bring (present 1st sg.; = traigo)
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men')
coraçón: coraçón — heart (= corazón) · also por coraçón 'willingly, heartily, with a will' (lo an por coraçón) · also de coraçón 'heartily, with a will' (adóbanse de coraçón 'they arm with a will')
folgar: folgar — to rest, take ease (infinitive; = holgar)
pagar: pagar — to pay, to satisfy (infinitive; pagar se ya 'he would be satisfied'; por pagar 'still unpaid, yet to be paid'; = pagar, pagarse)
amor: amor — love; por amor de 'for the love of' · also amor — favour, grace of a lord toward his vassal (davos su amor 'he gives you his favour'; del rey he su amor 'I have the king's favour') · also amor — good will, consent (of a vassal to his lord's act; con vuestro amor 'with your good will')
feches: fazer — you do (present 2nd pl., a reduced form of fazedes; esto feches agora 'this you do now'; the sense is clear, the exact derivation less so; = hacéis)
quitar: quitar — to leave, quit (infinitive; el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'; = quitar, closest abandonar) · also 'to set free' (quiero las i quitar 'I mean to free them there'; Pidal: 'libertar') · also quitar — to clear, remit (a charge; quitar lo mandava 'he ordered it cleared, i.e. paid or remitted'; quitar gelas 'to clear them for them')
essora: essora — then, at that moment (ess' + ora; en essora 'at that moment'; = entonces)
queredes: querer — you wish (present 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = queréis)
plazme: plazer + me — it pleases me (plaze + enclitic me; = me place)
afé: afé — behold, here is (presentative particle, used before a noun; afé Dios del çielo 'behold God of heaven'; = he aquí; origin uncertain) · also before a que-clause 'behold, (it is so) that' (afé que me plaz 'behold, it pleases me')
ojo: ojo — eye; a ojo 'in plain sight'
idlos: ir + los — go (id, imperative 2nd pl. of ir; = id) + los, object of the next verb conortar; idlos conortar 'go and comfort them' (= id a consolarlos)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another') · also d — 'about, concerning' (D' iffantes de Carrión yo vos quiero contar 'of the Infantes of Carrión I wish to tell you'; = de)
veremos: veer — we shall see (future 1st pl.; = veremos)
lidia: lidiar — he fights (present 3rd sg.; = lidia, closest lucha)
priso: prender — he took (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = prendió, tomó)
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year') · also de cabo — 'again, anew' (que los cometamos de cabo 'that we attack them again'; = de nuevo) · also a cabo de — at the end of, after (a cabo de tres sedmanas 'after three weeks') · also cabo — side, flank (del otro cabo 'from the other side'); fasta a cabo 'to the end' (de la cabeça fasta a cabo 'from head to tail'); a cabo 'to the end, along' (van a cabo, of men riding with the Cid; the shade is not certain); cabo — head, chief (de las otras es cabo 'it is the chief of the others')
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
albergada: albergada — encampment, camp (noun from albergar 'to lodge'; Pidal 'campamento'; esta albergada 'this camp'; = campamento)
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
amava: amar — he loved (imperfect 3rd sg.; lo que más amava 'what he loved most'; = amaba)
matava: matar — he was killing (imperfect 3rd sg.; = mataba)
astil: astil — shaft of a lance (= astil, asta)
metió: meter — he put (preterite 3rd sg.; metió mano 'laid hand to'; = metió)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping' · a mano 'by hand, hand-picked' (escollechos a mano 'chosen by hand') · dar de mano 'to let go, release' (Pidal 'soltar'; darvos e de mano 'I will let you go')
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied') · indirect: que non sabe qué se far '(so that) she knows not what to do'; avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also qué — how (exclamative before an adverb: qué bien pago 'how well he paid')
lidiava: lidiar — he was fighting (imperfect 3rd sg.; en campo lidiava 'he fought in the open field'; = lidiaba)
lança: lança — lance (= lanza); ardida lança, 'bold lance', stands for the bold man who wields it
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
fincava: fincar — he planted, pitched (imperfect) · also 'it remained, stayed' (imperfect 3rd sg.; todo el quinto a mio Çid fincava 'the whole fifth stayed with my Cid'; = quedaba)
aguijó: aguijar — he spurred (preterite) · also aguijar — he spurred on, pressed on (intransitive; aguijó cabadelant 'he spurred ahead'; Aguijó mio Çid 'the Cid pressed on')
bavieca: Bavieca — Babieca, the Cid's horse (proper name; = Babieca)
anda: andar — he goes, goes along (present 3rd sg.; = anda)
azes: az — battle lines, ranks (pl.; las azes de los moros 'the Moorish battalions'; = hileras, escuadrones)
aquesta: aquesta — this (fem. sg., reinforced demonstrative; = esta, archaic aquesta)
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o])
arrancada: arrancada — rout, headlong flight; also the pursuit and rout of the enemy (de arrancada 'in rout'; el arrancada, el before a vowel-initial fem. noun; = arrancada) · also 'victory' (Pidal's gloss at v. 1233: esta arrancada 'this victory') · also arrancar — won (past part. fem. sg. with aver, agreeing with lid: desta lid que mio Çid ha arrancada 'this battle my Çid has won'; = ganada)
alcança: alcançar — he overtakes, catches (present 3rd sg.; a los que alcança 'those whom he overtakes'; = alcanza)
veriedes: veer — you would have seen (conditional 2nd pl.; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
crebar: crebar — to break (infinitive; = quebrar); crebar albores 'dawn to break'
tantas: tanto — so many (fem. pl.; tantas lanças 'so many lances'; = tantas)
arrancarse: arrancar + se — to be pulled up, torn out (infinitive + reflexive se; arrancarse las estacas 'the pegs being torn up'; = arrancarse)
acostarse: acostar + se — to lean over, tilt, fall (infinitive + reflexive se; acostarse a todas partes los tendales 'the tent-poles leaning over on every side', Pidal 'ladearse, caerse'; = ladearse; not modern acostarse 'to lie down, go to bed')
tendales: tendal — tent-pole (pl.; Pidal: 'los postes sobre que están armadas las tiendas'; acostarse los tendales 'the tent-poles lean over and fall'; = postes de la tienda)
búcar: Búcar — Búcar, the Moorish king who comes against Valencia (personal name, Arabic; no modern Spanish form beyond Búcar)
sacan: sacar — they put out, post (present 3rd pl.; las arrobdas … sacan 'the patrols they send out'; = sacan)
